_setup: Static-token Atlassian MCP for HEADLESS / scheduled routines (Path A of loop-engineering).
The claude.ai OAuth connector does NOT survive a scheduled run (its token is in-memory per
session; a fresh scheduled connection is unauthenticated). This registers the community
'mcp-atlassian' server (sooperset), a local uvx subprocess that authenticates from a static
API token in its own env block — so it works unattended. See docs/loop-engineering.md.
Tool names differ from the OAuth connector: this server exposes snake_case tools
(mcp__mcp-atlassian__jira_search, jira_transition_issue, ...). atlassian-expert is
dual-bound and translates between the two vocabularies via a table in its agent doc.
PREREQS: uv/uvx installed (https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), Python 3.13 available to uvx.
STEPS:
1. Generate an Atlassian Cloud API token:
https://id.atlassian.com/manage-profile/security/api-tokens
No org-admin action is required — a personal API token is enough. (This is the whole
reason Path A targets this server instead of the Rovo MCP, which needs an admin to
enable token auth.)
2. Export the token in the routine's env (and your shell profile for interactive use) so it
is NEVER committed to the repo:
export JIRA_API_TOKEN='your-api-token'
3. Set JIRA_URL to your site and JIRA_USERNAME to the token owner's email below.
JIRA_URL must MATCH defaults.site in board-flow.yaml, or atlassian-expert's preflight
hard-fails (it refuses to run against the wrong Jira).
4. Copy the mcpServers block below into your HOST project's .mcp.json (NOT the plugin repo).
5. The site is fixed by JIRA_URL — there is NO cloudId to resolve.
6. Delete this _setup key from the real .mcp.json (it is ignored, but keep the file clean).
SECURITY: keep the token in the env var, not inline. A token written straight into a config
file is a committed credential one mistake away from a public repo — pass it by reference.
